Our 1st step in open source contribution to TamilNLP, I made a post late last
year on the open source contribution we are working on. Most of the current
research is focussed on Syntactic aspect of Tamil Language, we wanted to focus
on the semantic aspect of Tamil. சொல் திசையன் or Vaaku2vec released for Tamil
from data we have crawled through Tamil websites. The way the algorithm work
is fill in the blanks "I live in Tambaram and _______ to Adambakkam for work",
If we humans are asked to fill it we would fill it as commute, bike, drive
etc, the way we would come up with it is look at the surrounding words and
predict the missing word, algorithm works that way too. Similar words will be
near to each other in the vector space. I have posted some examples to show
what the algorithm learned. You can play with it in https://lnkd.in/gicCZ2S,
enter your own words and see what it is coming up with. If you want to
contribute to this open source, please reach out to Selvakumar Murugan,
Suriyadeepan Ramamoorthy or me. Code is open sourced in
https://lnkd.in/gjGn5YK. There is parallel development happening for Malayalam
too, reach out to Adam Shamsudeen if you want to contribute to it.

Harvard vs Hardwork? This was the question, raised by our own PM; Narendra
Modi. I didn't understand it then, but now I can understand the reasons. Why
the PM still deemed outsider in Lutyens Delhi? If he was a English speaking
guy with a snobbish background and a fancy degree, may be Lutyens Delhi would
have loved him. But, see the background from where our PM comes from. Was he
aware of IIT's or Harvard then? The pain that the PM reflected in his
statement; is the the pain of the millions of students of Tier 3/Tier 2
institutions? Companies are posting jobs and demanding tier 1 degree prior to
skills. The entire philosophy of skill based hiring is shaky, what is preached
here on LinkedIn. What about those who have spend 4 years slogging on
Codechef/ Kaggle? This is the reason why many tech start-ups hire a non-CS guy
(like mining, metallurgy) from a premier institution rather than a CS guy from
tier 1 or tier 3&2\. The reason is not to loose deep pockets and as well as
show the tag you have in your team. Ultimately, the ecosystem demands tag. I'm
not cribbing. Just I want, people who mentor students on LinkedIn, be
truthful. Deepak Kumar Nikhil Jain Ankur Warikoo Dr Aniruddha Malpani Aman
Goel What do you think? hashtag#tierdoesntmatter hashtag#frontbench

Andreessen & Paul Graham gives 10+ reasons and argues why doing a start-up is
really really tough. 1\. Startup puts you on an emotional rollercoaster. 2\.
Absolutely nothing happens, until you make it happen. 3\. You get told – NO a
lot. 4\. Hiring is a huge pain in the ass. 5\. The hours!! 5\. Finding out
what product to build. 7\. Building product. 8\. Taking it to the market. 9\.
It’s really easy for the culture of start-up to go sideways. 10\. Fear of
uncertainty. 11\. Don’t realize what you are avoiding. 12\. You are young and
inexperienced. Knows nothing about business. 13\. A family to support. 14\.
Parents’ want you to do to a job. What do you think now?
